questions: Do you experience excessive daytime sleepiness, falling asleep unintentionally during the day?
Do these sudden episodes of muscle weakness happen when you feel strong emotions like laughter, anger, or surprise?
During these episodes, do you remain fully aware of your surroundings?
Do you experience vivid dreams or hallucinations when falling asleep or waking up?
Do you ever feel unable to move your body for a few seconds when falling asleep or waking up (sleep paralysis)?
Have you ever had an episode of sudden weakness like this before?
Do you have a history of stroke, high blood pressure, or diabetes?
Were you feeling emotionally distressed or upset right before this happened?
Can you move your left arm and leg normally right now?
orders: Finger-stick blood glucose to check for hypoglycemia
CT scan of the head (non-contrast) to rule out hemorrhagic stroke
MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging to rule out acute ischemic stroke
Hoover's sign test (bedside examination for functional/paralytic vs organic hemiparesis)
Check blood pressure and pulse in both arms to rule out aortic dissection
Try to lift the patient's affected (left) leg while they attempt to lift the unaffected (right) leg against resistance (Hoover's sign test).
EEG (electroencephalogram) to rule out seizure activity
Lumbar puncture for CSF analysis (to rule out meningitis/encephalitis)
